items.stem: In observational drawing, the sight-size method is best described as:

options.text: Measuring the subject at its apparent size as seen on your picture plane, then matching that on the page
options.rationale: Correct: sight-size compares apparent sizes against a fixed viewpoint.

options.text: Drawing everything at exactly life-size regardless of distance
options.rationale: Sight-size uses apparent, not true, size.
That is not measured observational drawing.

options.text: Copying a photograph square by square
options.rationale: That is grid transfer, not sight-size.

items.explanation: Correct: sight-size compares apparent sizes against a fixed viewpoint.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO elements most directly create the illusion of three-dimensional volume on a flat surface? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A consistent range of values describing light and shadow
options.rationale: Correct: value gradation models form under light.

options.text: Core shadow and cast shadow placed by a single light source
options.rationale: Correct: coherent light logic reads as volume.

options.text: Using only outline with no interior tone
Filling shapes with one flat mid-grey everywhere
options.rationale: Uniform tone removes the sense of light.

items.explanation: Correct: value gradation models form under light.

items.stem: A beginner's cube looks 'wrong' because its receding edges stay parallel. The fix is to:

options.text: Converge the receding edges toward vanishing points on the horizon
options.rationale: Correct: linear perspective converges parallel edges to vanishing points.

options.text: Make all edges exactly the same length

options.rationale: Value does not fix the drawing error.
Line weight does not create recession here.

items.explanation: Correct: linear perspective converges parallel edges to vanishing points.
